narr: A strong developing system over brought moist southerly winds across the north and central Georgia, creating isolated severe thunderstorms and flash flooding on the afternoon and evening of January 3rd. The severe weather threat continued into Wednesday, January 4th, as the storm progressed eastward and brought a cold front across the area, producing isolated damaging wind gusts.
ev: The Emergency Manager reported flooding at the intersections of Union Grove Road at Creel Drive and Huey Road at Industrial Access Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing local creeks and rivers to overflow into the surrounding areas.

The Broadcast Media reported Glenn Street closed due to flooding after a car stalled in the floodwaters. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported multiple roads closed due to flooding, including Hardin Road, Shilo Road and Mountain Home Loop. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, resulting in flash flooding and rises in local area creeks and streams.

Broadcast Media reported the right lanes blocked on Interstate 285 at Peachtree Industrial Blvd due to water over the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Broadcast Media reported the closure of Valor Christian Academy due to flooding of the cafeteria, hallways and front entrance from the combination of heavy rainfall and backed up drains. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flooding.
The Athens Banner Herald reported flooding inside their office building on S Milledge Avenue. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a water rescue near the intersection of Crossville Road and Mansell Road due to high water on Hog Wallow Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain occurred quickly over the area, resulting in the rises of local creeks and streams.

The Emergency Manager reported a portion of Fannie Thompson Road was flooded by high water from Wildcat Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area, resulting in increased runoff into the creek and causing flash flooding.

Public reported Mansell Road and Highway 92 closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred in the area, producing rises on local creeks and streams and resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager relayed reports of flooding along Dean Hill Road, cutting off residential driveways. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency manager reported Horseshow Circle was washed out in Rockmart, and several other roads closed, including Brock Road, Stringer Road, Grady Road, and White River Road. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 to 5 inches fell quickly over the area, causing rises on local creeks and streams and flash flooding of flood-prone areas.
